                    ### Question
                    A 26-year-old woman comes to the physician because she has not had a menstrual period for 5 weeks. Menarche was at the age of 14 years and menses occurred at regular 30-day intervals. She reports having unprotected sexual intercourse 3 weeks ago. A urine pregnancy test is positive. Which of the following best describes the stage of development of the embryo at this time?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Sexual differentiation has begun, but fetal movement has not started
opb. Fetal heart is beating, but cardiac activity is not yet visible on ultrasound
opc. Limb buds have formed, but fetal movements have not begun
opd. Neural crest has formed, but limb buds have not yet formed
ope. Implantation has occured, but notochord has not yet formed

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
At 5 weeks post-menstruation, a positive urine pregnancy test indicates that implantation has occurred. At this stage, the embryo is typically in the early development phase, around 5-6 weeks gestation. By this time, the fetal heart is beginning to beat, but cardiac activity may not yet be visible on ultrasound. Limb buds usually start to form around this time, but fetal movements have not yet begun. Therefore, the best description of the embryo's development at this time is that the fetal heart is beating, but cardiac activity is not yet visible on ultrasound.
